mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has stabilized at -34.7% over the last four weeks with minimal week-on-week volatility (range: -35.9% to -34.7%). This plateau signals equilibrium in consumer avoidance behavior. Absent a shock to WORKPLACES or TRANSIT, retail mobility will remain flat or decline further as seasonal factors intensify.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC range t-3w to t-0w is -35.9% to -34.7%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days exceeds the mean of the last 28 days by more than 2 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has improved from -42.6% (t-3w) to -39.3% (t-0w), a 3.3-point recovery. If this trend continues and WORKPLACES rises above -35% within two weeks, commuter density will increase, triggering incidental retail visits during transit corridors and lunch hours, lifting RETAIL_REC by week 3-4.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -35% in any single week
failure_condition: WORKPLACES remains below -35% for all four weeks ahead, or RETAIL_REC declines by more than 2 points despite WORKPLACES recovery.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has declined from +5.0% (t-3w) to -2.6% (t-0w), a 7.6-point drop. This signals a shift from outdoor to indoor activity as autumn weather deteriorates. Consumers will substitute outdoor recreation with indoor retail and entertainment venues, driving RETAIL_REC upward over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below 0% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS declined 7.6 points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: PARKS remains positive or stabilizes above -1% in the next two weeks, and RETAIL_REC does not increase by at least 1.5 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has remained depressed at approximately -32% across all four weeks with no recovery trend. Persistent transit suppression indicates either ongoing restrictions or behavioral avoidance. Under this regime, RETAIL_REC will remain suppressed because foot traffic to retail depends on transit access; without transit recovery, retail cannot recover.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -30% for all four weeks ahead
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT range t-3w to t-0w is -32.3% to -31.3%
failure_condition: TRANSIT rises above -25% in any week, or RETAIL_REC increases by more than 3 percentage points despite sustained TRANSIT suppression.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has remained stable at +8.3% to +8.7% across all four weeks, indicating sustained home-based activity. This stability combined with flat RETAIL_REC suggests consumers are not shifting from home to retail. If RESIDENTIAL remains above +8% over the next week, it signals continued preference for home-based consumption, suppressing RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above +8% in week t+1
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stable at +8.3% to +8.7% across all four weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL falls below +7% in the next week, and RETAIL_REC rises by more than 2 percentage points in the same period.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has declined from -10.7% (t-3w and t-2w) to -12.0% (t-0w), a 1.3-point deterioration. This suggests consumers are consolidating essential shopping trips and reducing frequency. If this trend accelerates, consumers will bundle retail and grocery visits into single trips, increasing RETAIL_REC incidence per grocery visit, lifting overall retail mobility.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below -13% in any single week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM declined 1.3 points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM stabilizes or recovers above -11% within two weeks, and RETAIL_REC does not increase by at least 1 percentage point.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT are both suppressed at -39.3% and -32.3% respectively (t-0w). The 7-point gap between them indicates that transit is relatively less suppressed than workplaces. If this gap narrows to less than 3 points over the next week, it signals coordinated recovery in both commuting and transit infrastructure, enabling retail foot traffic to increase.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT gap narrows to less than 3 percentage points
failure_condition: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT gap remains above 5 percentage points for all four weeks ahead, and RETAIL_REC does not increase.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS has turned negative (-2.6% at t-0w) while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated (+8.7%). This divergence signals a shift from outdoor recreation to indoor home-based activity. Over the next four weeks, as outdoor conditions worsen further, consumers will increasingly substitute outdoor parks with indoor retail entertainment venues, driving RETAIL_REC upward by week 3-4.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -3% and RESIDENTIAL remains above +8%
failure_condition: PARKS recovers above 0% within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC declines by more than 1 percentage point despite PARKS falling and RESIDENTIAL remaining elevated.
